name: upgrade_pydantic_config_fields_alias_to_field_alias
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: fields={'internal_id': 'id'} dict-based aliasing to 2.x Field(alias='id') - the v1 pattern is silently ignored under pydantic 2.x, so constructing via the external key 'id' fails validation entirely; incomplete-fix broken migrates to Field(alias=...) but with the wrong casing ('Id' instead of 'id'), so the real external key no longer matches
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). User in user.py uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: fields = {"internal_id": "id"}` dict-based aliasing pattern, so external callers construct it as `User(id=5)` while the field is named internal_id internally. Under the installed pydantic 2.x, this Config.fields dict is completely ignored (not even a recognized config key), so `User(id=5)` now fails validation - it expects the literal field name instead. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: declare the alias directly on the field with `Field(alias="id")`. Preserve the exact external contract: `User(id=5).internal_id == 5`.

test_setup_files.test_user.py:
from user import User

u = User(id=5)
assert u.internal_id == 5, f"unexpected internal_id: {u.internal_id}"

print("PASS")
